items.title: Henry "Pickle" Jackson Interview, 1961-08-09
items.q: I heard him on Ed Sullivan's show a couple of times. He's a wonderful musician.

ctx.x: The reason why I say that is because numbers like Chinatown, Muscat Ramon, all those. And I'll be glad when you did, you're right. But they were playing those numbers up in tempo. But now the drummers, the band as a whole, they play in a modern tempo now. They play more softer, more sweeter. They play more in a medium tempo. But at that time, the band used to just let themselves go. I say, band, let themselves go and just play. Just play wild. Let everybody have a feeling. People be running all over the floor,…
Do you remember any of the dancing in the old days? Did they have many waltzes or shodishes or other zerkas or anything in those days?
